business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1) and P4 (10-Q MD&A)
business_model.claim: Kingstone sells property and casualty insurance products, primarily personal lines (homeowners, dwelling fire, condo/tenant, renters, personal umbrella), to individual consumers in New York through retail and wholesale agents and brokers via its subsidiary KICO.
quotes: We offer property and casualty insurance products through our wholly-owned subsidiary, Kingstone Insurance Company ("KICO").
KICO is a New York domiciled carrier writing business through retail and wholesale agents and brokers.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1, Product Lines section)
business_model.claim: Personal lines policies accounted for 94.7% of gross written premiums for the year ended December 31, 2025, with livery physical damage at 5.2% and other lines at 0.02%.
quotes: Personal lines policies accounted for 94.7% of our gross written premiums for the year ended December 31, 2025.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 and P3 (10-K), corroborated by F2 income statement line items
business_model.claim: Revenue derives from five sources: net premiums earned, ceding commission revenue from quota share reinsurance, net investment income, net realized gains or losses on investments, and other income (installment fees, reinstatement fees, NSF fees).
quotes: We derive substantially all of our revenue from KICO, including revenues from earned premiums, ceding commissions from quota share reinsurance, net investment income generated from our investment portfolio, and net realized gains and losses on investment securities.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1) and P3 (10-K MD&A)
business_model.claim: All insurance policies are 12-month terms; premiums are collected upfront and earned ratably over the coverage period, with the unearned portion carried as a liability and invested in the interim to generate investment income.
quotes: All of our policies are 12 month policies; therefore, a significant period of time can elapse between the receipt of insurance premiums and the payment of insurance claims.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1) and P3 (10-K MD&A); figure from F2
business_model.claim: Quota share reinsurance treaties transfer a portion of policy risk to reinsurers in exchange for ceding commission revenue that subsidizes the company's fixed operating costs.
quotes: Quota share reinsurance treaties transfer a portion of the profit (or loss) associated with the subject insurance policies to the reinsurers.

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (10-K MD&A); figure from F2 income statement
business_model.claim: Loss and loss adjustment expenses (LAE) are the single largest expense item, representing the estimated cost of settling policyholder claims plus adjusting costs such as adjuster fees and legal expenses.
quotes: Loss and LAE incurred represent our largest expense item, and for any given reporting period include estimates of future claim payments, changes in those estimates from prior reporting periods and costs associated with investigating, defending and servicing claims.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K) and P6 (press release)
business_model.claim: The net combined ratio (loss and LAE ratio plus net underwriting expense ratio) is the key measure of underwriting profitability; a ratio below 100% indicates underwriting profit before investment income.
quotes: A combined ratio under 100% indicates that an insurance company is generating an underwriting profit prior to the impact of investment income.

business_model.claim: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, 98.5% of KICO's direct premiums written came from New York policies, reflecting extreme geographic concentration.
quotes: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, 98.5% and 98.1% of KICO's direct premiums written came from the New York policies.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1) and P3 (10-K MD&A); California licensing from P4
business_model.claim: Cosi Agency, a multi-state licensed general agency subsidiary, generates net commission revenue by receiving ceding commissions from KICO on policies it places with other carriers and paying commissions to those agencies, retaining the spread.
quotes: Cosi retains the profit between the commission revenue received and the commission expense paid.

business_model.basis: stated in P3 and P4; absence of segment reporting observed across all provided filings
business_model.claim: The company operates as a single integrated P&C insurance business without separately reported operating segments; the holding company earns investment income from its cash holdings while KICO (and now KAIC) conduct the insurance operations.
quotes: Our holding company earns investment income from its cash holdings.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Recent Developments) and P2 (10-K Risk Factors)
business_model.claim: KICO's catastrophe reinsurance program has a top limit of $440,000,000 (equivalent to a 1-in-100 year storm event), with a 5% quota share retention of $5,500,000 per occurrence effective January 1, 2026, and 100% reinsurance above that layer up to the limit.
quotes: KICO increased the top limit of its catastrophe reinsurance coverage from $280,000,000 to $440,000,000, which, equates to a 1-in-100 year storm event according to the primary industry catastrophe model that we follow.

Effective January 1, 2026, $10,000,000 of losses in a catastrophe are subject to a quota share reinsurance treaty, which covers 5% of catastrophe losses such that we retain $5,500,000 of risk per catastrophe occurrence.
